Use-case / asks (from calls):
- Primary use: in-app chat for SMB dashboard (support + context-aware assistant).
- Latency priority: UX sensitive; want <500ms typical, accept occasional spikes but need improvements vs current 1.1s p95.
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget; wants minimal lift (hosted API) before thinking Dedicated.
- Model preference: open to small/medium open models; curious about quantized variants for cost.
- Routing/fallback: want simple fallback to smaller model on bursts.
- Security: basic audit logs; SSO not required now.

Observed problems / diagnostics from logs:
- Traffic mostly NA/EU with a small APAC tail. EU requests routed to eu-west but tests show higher serialization time from their client bundles (~200-400ms).
- Prompt sizes average ~1200 tokens (system + memory + user history) — heavy.
- No streaming enabled on client; full-response wait until token generation completes.
- Client-side timeouts set low (8s) causing occasional mid-response cancellations; server-side SLOs appear fine.

Redwood tuning suggestions provided in call + to-do: (what AE/SE recommended)
- Region choice: encourage routing nearest region (us-east-1 for NA, eu-west-1 for EU). Run A/B test: route EU->eu-west-1 vs eu-central to compare tail latency — keep notes.
- Prompt/recall guidance: trim system messages, limit retained history to 3 turns, use retrieval to fetch only a short context (summarize prior convo). Aim to reduce prompt to <600 tokens for fast responses.
- Streaming: enable streaming responses in the client to improve perceived latency (render tokens as they arrive).
- Timeouts/retries: set client timeout to 20s for generation calls, retry idempotently for network errors with exponential backoff; avoid cancelling mid-stream.
- Model/config: try smaller / faster model variant for default chat (recommendation: redwood-1-small or similar fast profile), and keep redwood-1-medium for escalation. Consider q4_0 quantized instance for cost-sensitive paths.
- Caching & batching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (greetings, onboarding text). For high-concurrency bursts, use recommended batching thresholds in Optimize.
- Fallback policy: configure automatic fallback to small model when latency > threshold or capacity warnings.

2) 2026-03-15: Redwood to provide trial config (region routing + model presets + timeout settings) and a one-page tuning checklist.
